| [CLAIM-606](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-606.md) v2 | A localized structure can persist by an internal balance that needs no supply, by a balance of gain and loss that needs a standing supply, or by a topological charge that continuous change cannot remove, and the three differ in what carries the structure's identity, how it forms and how it ends; because thresholds and abrupt ends appear in all of them, even with no supply at all, only withdrawing the supply and measuring the outflow tells which route a structure is on | The assistant's, after the owner's hunch that "the physics/dynamics of soliton formation could be a valuable angle through which to consider some of our questions about individuation and persistence".   supply. They come in a family set by their initial data, and they keep
  their identity through collisions.
- Dissipative solitons are held by a supplied balance of gain and loss.
  Their shape is "predetermined by the equation parameters, rather than
  by the initial conditions", and they last "until the pump laser is
  switched off".
- Topological solitons carry a charge that continuous change cannot
  remove.
A fourth case, the oscillon, has none of the three protections.
